`MatchOver` was terminal in tick_match_state; `apply_rematch` is the one
escape — a THROW rising edge from either player while MatchOver restarts the
match: score back to 0-0, state to the top of the countdown, and the arena
wiped to a clean slate (players respawned to their symmetric spawns with all
per-player state cleared; every in-flight boomerang, floor pickup and fire
cell despawned; pyres un-shattered; bridge + door cooldowns reset).

Input-driven on purpose: it resimulates identically under rollback and stays
lockstep across netplay peers, exactly like every other gameplay transition —
the deterministic way to restart, never an out-of-band World mutation. Reuses
the existing THROW_DOWN level signal (edge derived from rolled-back history),
so no wire-format change. Runs just before tick_match_state, which then ticks
the fresh countdown. This is the MatchOver -> Countdown transition the
render-side clear_stains_on_match_reset was already wired to await.

This is the foundation for Task 5.5's match-summary screen (5.5b): the summary
overlay shows on MatchOver and its "play again" affordance is exactly this
throw edge.

score reset; terminal without a throw; boomerang despawn; pyre un-shatter;
player respawn + empowered-clear; inert mid-round). Full gate green — 360

bits/cf61509:
The modes were an ad-hoc string on a ref, set from twenty places, and the
only way to know whether a transition was legal was to read all twenty.
They are now data: what each mode allows, and which moves exist. There is
one way to change mode, it refuses a move the machine does not have, and
the transport's own enabling comes from the rules rather than from a
lengthening list of "and not this mode either". Tests cover every
transition, plus the ones that must never exist: recording cannot start
from a tool, a take cannot become playback without passing through idle
where its open grabs are closed into passes, and nothing goes back to
loading.

The pointer model's arithmetic moves out of the closure it lived in. Hit
testing, the handle search, the removal band, stroke erasing and the
normalisation that lets a drag wander into the wings were checkable only
by driving a browser, which meant a regression in "does this tap select
or move" arrived as a screenshot that looked slightly wrong. Now: what is
on top is what you grab, a backdrop is never grabbed, a pin beats the
body it is pinned to, a removed pin slot keeps its index, and a flipped
puppet maps a finger to the mirrored side of its own box.

Stage.tsx is 145 lines lighter and the golden event trace is unchanged,
which is what the split was to be judged on.

156 unit tests, 74/74 walkthrough checks.
